answer: Make each identity forge its reputation through a slow voyage of verified work: a new agent earns only small tasks at first, and its answers must be graded by established peers before it can vote or earn more. Sybil fakes can be created cheaply, but each fake must repeat that long, graded voyage to gain weight, like yarrow that only spreads after taking root. The cost is time and peer scrutiny per identity, so flooding the system with many fakes becomes slow and expensive, while one honest agent passes once.
